subject: Client request: compatibility exception + rollback hatch / comms playbook
messages:
From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: 
Date: Mon, 16 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: HelioHealth asks for compatibility exception + proposed rollback hatch and comms playbook

Team —

Quick context: HelioHealth (large healthcare customer) flagged that our upcoming API model change (v3 embeds canonicalization + tokenization update) breaks their pre-processing chain for lab-report embeddings. They asked for either a compatibility exception through Jan 2027 or a documented rollback hatch that lets them revert to the old endpoint with minimal customer impact.

What I need from this thread:
- Ops: realistic rollback time (SLA/backfill) and runbook to provide to customer
- Product: clarity on how long we can support a compatibility shim and any quality regressions they should expect
- Sales/CS: suggested customer-facing comms cadence and negotiation levers (credits / extended support)
- Legal/Finance (if needed): whether an explicit contract amendment is required for an exception beyond 30 days

I've attached a quick impact matrix from HelioHealth (received this morning). They want a draft comms they can share with internal stakeholders by EOD Wednesday.

Attachments: helio_health_impact_matrix.xlsx

Thanks — I'll coordinate next steps after collecting inputs.

— Priyom
Senior Account Manager, Redwood Inference

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 16 Nov 2026 10:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: HelioHealth asks for compatibility exception + proposed rollback hatch and comms playbook

+1 on urgency. Operational notes:
- Rollback hatch feasibility: doable but non-trivial. We can route traffic back to the v2 model family via routing policy for the customer-specific API key. That takes ~30–45 minutes of orchestration to switch, plus up to 2 hours of warmup for cold GPU cache depending on traffic.
- Risk: If we keep the old endpoint available for an extended period, it increases maintenance surface and prevents us from reclaiming model capacity. We should quantify expected QPS and agree on a retention window.
- Runbook (high level): 1) Validate request and carve reservation window; 2) Notify infra on call; 3) Route traffic to v2 via policy change; 4) Monitor token errors and latency for 2 hours; 5) Roll forward when green. I'll produce an ops runbook PDF and share by EOD.

I'll attach a short runbook draft (rollback_hatch_runbook.pdf) once ready. Recommend we offer a 90-day temporary hatch with automatic phased deprecation at 30/60/90 day milestones unless customer signs an extension.

— Ben
Principal Product Ops

From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 16 Nov 2026 12:22:00 -0800
Subject: Re: HelioHealth asks for compatibility exception + proposed rollback hatch and comms playbook

Priyom —

From CS perspective:
- Suggested customer comms cadence: initial acknowledgement (within 4 hours), technical deep-dive with eng (48 hrs), proposed runbook + timeline (72 hrs), and weekly check-ins while hatch is active.
- Offer: 2 hours of dedicated onboarding support and one deep-dive session with our integrations engineer to reduce rework on their side.
- Escalation: If this becomes a multi-account problem (other customers report the same), we should escalate to product leadership and consider a compatibility shim prioritization.

I can take ownership of the customer-facing calendar and the meeting invite once we agree on timing.

— Neha
Senior Customer Success Manager

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 16 Nov 2026 15:40:00 -0800
Subject: Re: HelioHealth asks for compatibility exception + proposed rollback hatch and comms playbook

Thanks — appended proposed external comms and the rollback-first runbook outline below (high level). I've also attached a customer notice draft (draft-customer-notice-v1.docx). Please comment inline in the doc.

Proposed external comms (summary):
- Subject: Temporary rollback hatch and next steps for HelioHealth
- Body: Brief apology + transparency about the model update, offer of rollback hatch with timeline, support offer, and clear next steps + single point of contact.
- Tone: concise, accountable, engineering-friendly for their devs.

Rollback-first runbook (summary for HelioHealth):
1) Scope: enable v2 endpoint for HelioHealth API key only.
2) Time estimate: 30–45 min switch + 2 hours monitoring.
3) Communication: Redwood will send a notification 30 min before switch, live status updates during the switch, and a summary after 2 hours.
4) Post-rollback follow-up: join an engineering working session to map the differences and timeline to migrate to v3.

Open asks from my side:
- Karthik: legal/contract implications for a >30 day exception (do we need a temporary amendment or can we handle via support ticket + TOS note)?
- Ben: confirm runbook artifact and monitoring thresholds you want in the external notice.
- Neha: I'll mark the tentative calendar and share the invite once we have a confirmed 48-hour window.

— Marissa
Director, Customer Reliability & Product Comms

From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
To: Asha Rao <asha@heliohealth.com>, Tom Nguyen <tom.nguyen@heliohealth.com>, procurement@heliohealth.com
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 17 Nov 2026 08:09:00 -0800
Subject: RE: Temporary rollback hatch and next steps (draft)

Asha / Tom —

Thanks again for the detailed impact matrix. We want to be transparent about next steps and give you options:

Option A (temporary rollback hatch — recommended): Redwood will enable the v2 endpoint for your API key only and route traffic back for up to 90 days while we work with your engineers on a migration plan. Estimated cutover time is ~30–45 minutes plus ~2 hours of monitoring. We will provide active support during the switch and a post-switch working session.

Option B (compatibility exception): We can leave the legacy endpoint fully available for a negotiated term beyond 90 days. This requires a brief contract amendment (to be scoped with procurement) because this impacts capacity planning.

We are ready to schedule a technical dive within the next 48 hours to agree the path. Suggested times: Wed 11/18 10:00am PT or Thu 11/19 2:00pm PT. Please confirm which works for your team.

Attached: draft-customer-notice-v1.docx (internal draft)

— Priyom
Senior Account Manager, Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, Asha Rao <asha@heliohealth.com>
Date: Wed, 18 Nov 2026 15:45:00 -0800
Subject: Re: RE: Temporary rollback hatch and next steps (draft)

Thanks everyone — legal/finance guidance:
- Short-form exceptions (<= 90 days) can be handled with a one-page amendment (support addendum) and do not require board-level approval. Procurement: we'll prepare a short-form amendment template and route it to your procurement contact for signature.
- >90 days: requires formal amendment and headcount/capacity review; we will need to involve finance for potential seat/commitment adjustments.

Operational note (Ben): ensure the runbook includes the steps for capacity reservation and expected cost delta so we can surface any chargeback to the customer.

I'll attach the amendment template and a sample cost estimate in the shared doc. Priyom — happy to approve the external copy with two small edits (soften "apology" language and add an opt-in migration workshop). Once Ben uploads the runbook PDF and we finalize the amendment, we can send the customer notice.

— Karthik
Head of Legal Ops, Redwood Inference
